status: DRAFT v3 by akiendell_cc_0, 2026-11-14, for re-charting by akienasus. Not cast. v3 REPLACES v1/v2 after finding that most of this ticket's code already exists: the remaining work is wiring, and it depends on a child that feeds it.
title: the existing gate-feedback probe is wired: a gate firing is recorded and a scheduled inspection reaches the model through an injected resolver
wanted: yes, measured 2026-11-14: its producer and its door both exist now. cairn/tools/data_recorder (PROVED, ticket 3ca32dd07e86) is written as 'the passive consumer's mailbox ... scheduled-llm-gate-inspection reads the accumulated records and proposes parameter adjustments'; cairn/tools/base/gate_class.py:201 TransitionGate.adjust(sieve_name, dial, value) returns the prior state, so a rollback exists; outline 17.7 (data_recorder: a mailbox until an inspection reads them), 17.10 (feedback) and 5.9 (Cairn's scheduled list: a pulse matches an entry and kicks off a probe) carry the pieces. The ticket's own horizon ('after the feedback tool's route is built ... at least one gate collects structured feedback') is the open part: not measured here whether any gate writes into a data_recorder yet.
superseded_by: none found: grep of CairnCommons/tickets for 'scheduled-llm-gate-inspection' and 'gate inspection' finds only 3ca32dd07e86 (its producer, PROVED) and this ticket.
intention: The gate_parameters_adjust_from_feedback probe (cairn/tools/base/probes/) reads feedback that gate firings really write, is handed a resolver that asks the language model through the inference proxy, and its proposals still land only through TransitionGate.adjust, recording the prior value so the same door puts it back. Nothing new is invented: the existing inspect/build_prompt/parse_proposals are the implementation.
why: A sieve that matches 100% cannot show efficacy; the feedback it collects is where efficacy hides and nobody reads it. Reading it on a schedule closes the loop (measure, accumulate, read, adjust, measure differently). Original statement and Law 4 / learns-its-gates tracing in the b0c0c47835c1 ticket.
traces_to: Law 4 (a gate whose dials never adjust from evidence is policy dressed as physics), Law 6 (the gate's own door is the only write path), sieves-measure-not-judge (the model proposes, never decides, never sits in the measurement path), Law 1 (reading accumulated feedback once instead of a human re-reading it each session).

clauses.claim: with the child ticket's recorder fed, the probe's trigger reads those records and fires once the threshold is met, and a firing with a stub resolver returns the proposals and the prior values adjust() returned
with a resolver injected by the shim, _carry no longer answers 'no resolver in context'; with none it still refuses loudly and applies nothing
an adjustment applied through the probe is undone by calling adjust with the recorded prior value, restoring the dial exactly (the existing revert tooth, now through the probe)
the model is never in a sieve's measurement path: the probe imports no inference code (the resolver is injected) and the module has no loop, thread or daemon

decisions.text: D1: REUSE, do not add a module. The change is inside cairn/tools/base/probes/gate_parameters_adjust_from_feedback.py: _read_feedback reads the recorder the child ticket feeds (DataRecorder.read()) instead of BUILD_GATE._feedback_dir files; inspect, build_prompt and parse_proposals stay.

D2: the shim that fires the probe injects context['resolver'], a callable that asks the inference proxy over the bus; the probe imports no inference code. Which shim carries it follows the holder chosen in the child ticket (codemother).

D3: CADENCE, a CC call recorded as a decision. Outline 5.9, 17.7 and 17.10 name no tier or sleep for a gate inspection (5.9.3.1: a pulse matches a list entry and kicks off a probe; 17.7: a mailbox 'until an inspection reads them'). The probe keeps its existing records-accumulated threshold as its trigger, and its firing is the daily sleep entry (5.3.3.1, 5.3.3.4: the clock, 2300), since it reads accumulated feedback and the model call belongs in the box's opening.

D4: extend the existing proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_gate_feedback.py with the probe's teeth under this ticket's PROVES key (clauses 1 to 4), over a scratch recorder and a stub resolver; red first.

out: gate_class.py (the child ticket changes how feedback is written)

measured.saw: MOST OF b0c0 IS ALREADY BUILT, so v1 and v2 of this plan (a new gate_inspection.py module) would have paralleled it (Law 1). cairn/tools/base/probes/gate_parameters_adjust_from_feedback.py already has _read_feedback, build_prompt, parse_proposals, inspect(records, resolver) which calls BUILD_GATE.adjust per proposal, a Threshold and an enough() predicate; cairn/tools/base/gate_class.py TransitionGate._collect_feedback already writes a structured record after EVERY gate firing (gate, timestamp, verdict, checks_total/passed/failed, record, mismatches); adjust() returns the prior state and cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_gate_feedback.py covers green/red feedback, adjust, revert and the refusals. What is missing is the WIRING, both measured: (1) _collect_feedback writes only when self._tree is set, and `.construct(` has no caller outside proofs (git grep), so BUILD_GATE._tree is None in production and no feedback is ever written: find ~/.cairn for a feedback dir returns none on akiendell, and the Dell has no gate recorder either (orchestrator 2026-11-14: records.jsonl only in codemother/0/tools/charter/inbound (302) and inferenceproxy/0/tools/data_recorder/metrics (18)); (2) the probe's _carry needs context['resolver'] and nothing in the repo injects one (it answers 'no resolver in context'). Note also that the probe reads BUILD_GATE._feedback_dir (files), not a data_recorder, though cairn/tools/data_recorder/intention+why.json says gate feedback lands there (17.7).
measured.how: read the probe, gate_class.py, test_gate_feedback.py; git grep '.construct(' and 'resolver'; find ~/.cairn for feedback dirs and records.jsonl; the orchestrator's Dell count

unmeasured: whether the probe is armed/registered with a shim anywhere (not read); the shape of the resolver verb on the inference proxy (outline-level, not read here); no real model call is exercised by any tooth
